about: Clay's body (neck, torso, tail, then limbs and wings), element by element (see body_sheets.md). Model units: z = (700 - px) / 343, y = (830 - py) / 343, from the 1400 px side sheet; x = Clay's left. The bind pose is the side sheet's pose, so the side view can be checked against the sheet directly; the tail's lower run is lifted onto the ground and curls toward the viewer (+x).

trunk.note: Neck, torso and tail are one continuous mass, built as one loft along a curved spine with cross-sections perpendicular to it. Measured on the side sheet (trunk_overlay): the spine was traced through the middle of the body, and at each station the depth to the dorsal outline (top of neck and back, outer edge of the tail curl) and to the ventral outline (throat, chest, belly, inner edge of the tail curl) was measured along the perpendicular. The neck is short and thick, the torso a deep barrel (~0.9 from back to belly), the tail thick (~0.25-0.38) nearly to its tip.

width.note: half-width = factor * mean depth; widths are not in the side sheet: from the official front and three-quarter art (a broad barrel chest, thick neck)

zones.note: On the neck and torso the zone edges are measured side-view lines, not fractions. The dark edge is the line of small square plates: from behind the ear it runs back and then straight DOWN the side of the neck into the shoulder, round the bottom of the dark shoulder patch, and back along the wing arm. The cream edge bounds the wide throat band, down the front of the neck into the chest; behind the forelegs the cream rises to meet the dark edge (no orange band). On the tail (after lines_until_s) the edges are side fractions.

tail_pose.note: the sheet draws the tail's lower run below the feet (it lies nearer the viewer); in 3D it rests on the ground and curls toward the viewer

bones.note: spine bones by ranges of s; the head bone attaches to the last neck bone

sculpt.note: Muscle masses sculpted into the trunk, and colour patches over them (mirrored). The shoulder is not a separate piece: the scapula and deltoid swell the side of the chest over the top of the upper arm, and the dark back runs down over it as a rounded patch (side sheet px 400-575, py 380-532), rimmed below by small square plates.

front_leg.note: Measured on the side sheet's near front leg (fleg crop, px 330-700, py 380-870): a big dark rounded shoulder mass rimmed below by small square plates; a heavy orange upper arm running down and back to an elbow that points backward (~0.64 long); a forearm column angling down and forward to a low wrist (~0.67), cream along its back; a compact hand (~0.3) with three big hooked dark claws and a dewclaw high on the back of the wrist. The sheet's far leg steps forward; the rest pose uses the near leg's pose on both sides. Thickness: the upper arm is a huge muscular mass (about 0.5 deep near the shoulder), the forearm a heavy column; the shoulder sits on the outside of the broad chest.
front_leg.aspect_note: side-to-side width over front-to-back depth of each section (the hand is broad and flat)

cream_back.note: along the back of the forearm and wrist (fraction of the limb's length; width as a fraction of the half-circumference)

hind_leg.note: Measured on the side sheet (tail crop): the hind leg is drawn in a deep crouch. The thigh, mostly hidden behind the wing, runs down from the hip to a low knee (~px 895, py 720); the shin runs back to the heel near the ground (~px 1090, py 812), cream down its back; the long digitigrade foot runs forward from the heel along the ground to the ball of the foot (~px 900) with dark square studs along its top; four longer, splayed toes with claws; a spur claw at the heel points back. Thigh muscle mass from the official art (How to Draw, limited edition): a big rounded orange haunch.

carapace.note: The dark back is not paint: like the head's roof it is a shell fitted over the trunk, standing proud of it, a turtle-shell carapace. Transverse bands (~0.09-0.12 apart on the sheet) wrap over the top down to the rim; the rim is a row of small square marginal scutes along the measured dark edge, their outer edges rolled outward like a turtle shell's margin. It runs from behind the head down the tail.
